title: Attack rolls and d20
description: Attack quality compares the d20 total, including bonuses, against target evasion. A margin of -10 or less is evaded; below 0 is a glancing hit; 0 to 9 is a hit; 10 or more is a critical hit. The attack definition can upgrade or downgrade the result for natural rolls. Recent rolls retain the actual dice and bonus.

title: Damage resolution
description: An attack rolls its raw damage, adds flat source damage, applies outgoing bonuses and attack quality, then applies target defenses. Armor reduces the combined physical hit. Matching resistances apply afterward. The combat journal links to the stages and typed values actually recorded for that attack.

title: Effects and periodic damage
description: Effects belong to the combat result and are not automatically applied by a damage type. Periodic damage retains the source snapshot captured when the effect was applied; current target defenses are read when resolving a tick. Flat attack damage is not added again to each periodic tick.

title: Targets and combat state
description: Left-click a living target to select it. Click the same target or the ground to clear selection. The top bar shows the selected target and its health. Minimap markers distinguish living and defeated bodies. Overhead bars can be changed in Settings.

title: Attacks, skills and cooldowns
description: The current playable attack is a projectile. Accepted attacks pay their cost once and respect cooldowns. The remaining three skill slots are locked placeholders. A broad skill set, melee delivery and skill assignment are not implemented yet.

title: Spatial inventory
description: The bag has 12 columns and 5 rows without scrolling or automatic growth. Each item occupies its base rectangle. Dragging retains the cell you grabbed. Bounds, overlap and room for returning equipment are checked before a UI equipment change. Grid positions last for the current session; saving and item rotation are not implemented.

title: Main hand and offhand
description: The main-hand weapon and compatible offhand flank body armor. A bow permits a quiver; a one-handed weapon permits a shield. A shield can remain without a main weapon; a quiver cannot. Changing the main weapon returns incompatible offhand equipment and removes its bonuses in the same change. Both rings need different owned item instances.

title: Affixes and implicit properties
description: Every base has implicit properties, separate from rolled affixes. Implicit properties do not use affix capacity. Each affix retains its selected tier, d100 quality, actual values and available tier pool. Item cards show affixes normally; Alt adds captured ranges and quality details.

title: Affix tiers
description: T1 is the strongest numbered tier. Each affix has its own authored pool: it may end at T16, T15, T4 or another tier. Available tiers are shown from the actual captured pool. Current starter affixes only define T2; complete progression tables are not authored yet. Tier and item rarity are separate.

title: Affix quality and ranges
description: One d100 quality roll is shared by all values of a rolled affix. 1 maps to the selected tier minimum; 100 maps to its maximum, with intermediate values rounded at the authored precision. Advanced details show value [minimum/maximum] quality% tier. Inspecting an item never rerolls it.

title: Flat, Increased and More
description: Flat modifiers add amounts before percentage scaling. Increased modifiers add within their pool; More modifiers multiply separately. Global and typed damage increases share one additive pool. Percentage resistance points differ from a relative increase to resistance. Typed flat damage is added to attacks, not repeatedly to periodic ticks.

title: Item rarity and affix limits
description: Rarity sets the maximum number of affixes. Fewer affixes do not lower rarity automatically; adding affixes does not automatically upgrade it. Raising rarity is a separate operation whose gameplay recipes and costs remain future work. Each rarity entry shows the current configured capacity.

title: Linked explanations and pins
description: Underlined text opens a related explanation. Pin keeps a card after closing its source window. Drag a card header to move it. Escape closes the latest unpinned card; use its close button to remove a pin. Item rarity colors remain separate from the muted colors of damage types.

title: Controls and windows
description: Current gameplay bindings appear above Menu. Inventory and Character can stay open independently while the world continues. The reference, pause and settings stop the game while you read or edit. Search captures text input so typing does not toggle other windows.

title: Display, sound and overhead bars
description: Settings supports windowed/fullscreen mode, vertical synchronization, master volume and optional overhead bars for enemies and the player. Apply saves presentation preferences independently of a game run. Closing without applying discards edits. Language changes apply immediately and are saved with presentation preferences.

title: Restart and session persistence
description: Restart or starting a new game creates a fresh session. Equipped items, grid positions, combat history and pinned cards are not saved between runs. Presentation settings are stored separately.

title: Primary attributes and Luck
description: Primary-attribute progression, attribute-to-dice bonuses and Luck-driven item drops are planned and are not active in this playable prototype. The current sheet displays the resolved stats used by combat and movement. The reference does not invent numeric attribute bonuses or a finished progression table.
